My (and probably George’s too) favorite quote in this story came from (Supreme) Justice Stewart who, when asked to specify what exactly characterized a “profane, offensive word”, boldly and coldly declared: “I know it when I see it” … aka #supremeshit (*)! That’s what George went on to call out in his bold and hot way: the shocking hypocrisy of Supreme Court Justices, refusing to acknowledge the (lack of) of clarity and transparency of the new laws banning “profanities” from broadcast radio and television.  What’s striking to me is that, despite major technological progress, life (the universe, and everything:) is mostly the same… because we live in a world where most men fear to live in truth, and sadly, humanity remains at the mercy of rich, entitled, mostly white men characterized by a dire, unholy need for control, and heavy duty levels of contempt for transparency and accountability, in the name of democracy and justice aka #winwin games… Men as unable to acknowledge their own shortcomings, as unashamed to defend the hypocritical logic of unclear, unfair laws—men who tend to always “muddy the waters to make it seem deep”, as Nietzsche wisely observed.   *yet another proof some “things don’t change”,  and “it gets better” is a nice thing to say, but also often just cheap, shallow crap… Please pass the ironic grains of salt… and blessed be George Carlin!  — @bananasutra lyrics:  “7 Dirty Words”  Banjo strumming, a quirky tune, George Carlin’s words, under the moon. song_title: A Letter To My Friend (Never Again)
_desc-sc:
I mourn peace and freedom. I mourn checks and balances, and the democratic consensus. I mourn every innocent victim of war—every child, every dream crushed by every tyrant. How could I not? How can you not?  Being pro-people and pro-peace isn’t being anti-anyone, it’s refusing to let pain justify cruelty. I love my Jewish friends, but I also mourn the moral consensus we once called “Never Again.” Because safety matters—yours, mine, theirs, ours. Everyone’s safety matters… That’s why my heart can’t stop singing and praying for world peace. I’m not anti-anyone. I’m anti-dehumanization. My hope is that the Jewish story can end in healing, not repetition.   I can’t help but hope… because I believe we can protect each other without inflicting new wounds. Empathy isn’t a zero-sum game; it’s what makes us human! It’s what helps us survive and thrive as one earthly, democratic tribe. In fact, empathy is the ultimate weapon against evil! That is exactly why those who cannot feel it try to divide and conquer by calling empathy weak or dangerous.  Simone Weil wrote: “Imaginary evil is romantic; real evil is gloomy, monotonous, barren.” So when I hear friends glorify revenge to justify genocide, I weep… as if trauma could explain violence because it gives despair a proud story; as if moral drama, fueled by hubris, could heal the multigenerational void of helplessness left by past and future trauma. When a pacifist says “no more heroes, no more villains, just humans,” it’s treated as a threat, as if “you’re with us or against us” were unquestionable truth.
  But Nietzsche warned that those who fight monsters must be careful not to become them, and Hannah Arendt reminded us that fear of being a victim can make us accept the role of the oppressor. Real humanism doesn’t erase trauma, it transcends it! Pacifism isn’t naïve; it’s a radical commitment to ending the cycle of identification with force.   Winning means grounding ourselves in moral coherence. Life is sacred. It’s not about picking sides between nations (or parties)… it’s about choosing compassion over cruelty. Sigh.
  And so well now, of course, I wrote yet another song—another “Letter to My Friend,” about Never Again. 💌  — @bananasutra – Lyrics: “Letter to My Friend”  Hey love,
 I’ve been thinkin’, the air’s gone strange. We built a bridge, but fear made the range.
 When did caring turn into crime?
 Since when did heartbeats choose a side in time?  You think my tears forgot their tribe,
 But pain’s one language, that’s the vibe.
 If I cry for Gaza, do I leave you dry?
 Or can both our ghosts learn to sigh and fly?  I’m not your enemy, babe, I’m the echo that remains.
 Every love I add don’t steal your chains.
 Peace ain’t a prize that one can win;
 It’s a wound that heals when we let it begin.
 Oh, Bananasutra sings again…  Your roots run deep in haunted clay,
 I feel that tremor every day.
 But if walls keep empathy out of sight,
 Ain’t we just living in longer nights?  You guard your story like sacred wine,
 But I sip my sorrow... it tastes like thine.
 Can’t “never again” be a door, not a wall?
 Must one rise so another can fall?  I’m not your rival, love, I’m the ache that understands,
 Two trembling souls with open hands.
 My heart don’t subtract when it starts to expand;
 It multiplies truth in foreign lands.  Pain is pain; it don’t wear flags.
 It needs no borders, no tags.
 Fear’s a thief, babe, it steals our sight,
 Makes day look wrong and wrong look right.  Would you rather win, or rather heal?
 Would you rather numb, or rather feel?
 If trust could hum a new refrain,
 Would you hear my note through your pain?  I’m not against you, I’m just against cruel.
 Love ain’t a weapon; it’s the rebel’s rule.
 Let’s rewrite Never Again for all,
 ’Cause peace built on pride’s just another wall.  So hey, my friend, come dance instead?
 We’ll sing for the living, not just the dead.
 Bananasutra’s heart don’t bend,
 It blooms, it breaks, it mends. 🪽

song_title: A Man's a Man and A' That
_desc-sc:
EPx3 - VOL. 02  Robert Burns wrote “A Man’s a Man for A’ That” over 200 years ago, and guess what… not much has changed! In fact, it is statistically fair to say that the socio—economical divide is getting worse everyday, because greedy and entitled a-holes confuse privilege with rights, and don’t even think twice about the meaning or value of equality, human dignity, and justice. Blessed be Burns for daring to say what few would: wealth and status mean nothing—what truly matters is a person’s integrity, wisdom, and kindness. Personality, aka our “true color”, is so underrated…   Why his song matters: - In an era of rising inequality, where wealth and fame often overshadow true worth, Burns’ words remind us that status does not define a person. - As leaders and elites gain power through privilege, not merit, his message calls us to value wisdom, honesty, and justice above empty authority. - In a world that too often divides people by class, race, or borders, A Man’s a Man for A’ That stands as a timeless call for fairness, unity, and human dignity.  Burns saw beyond his time and envisioned a world where honor and intelligence, not gold and crowns, define greatness. That dream isn’t just history—it’s still worth singing for. Maybe now more than ever.  -- Robert Burns’s original lyrics: (Original Scots Version) Is there for honest Poverty
That hings his head, an’ a’ that?
The coward-slave, we pass him by,
We dare be poor for a’ that!
For a’ that, an’ a’ that,
Our toils obscure, an’ a’ that,
The rank is but the guinea’s stamp,
The man’s the gowd for a’ that. What though on hamely fare we dine,
Wear hoddin grey, an’ a’ that?
Gie fools their silks, and knaves their wine,
A man’s a man for a’ that:
For a’ that, an’ a’ that,
Their tinsel show, an’ a’ that;
The honest man, though e’er sae poor,
Is king o’ men for a’ that. Ye see yon birkie, ca’d a lord,
Wha struts, an’ stares, an’ a’ that;
Though hundreds worship at his word,
He’s but a coof for a’ that:
For a’ that, an’ a’ that,
His ribband, star, an’ a’ that,
The man o’ independent mind,
He looks an’ laughs at a’ that. Then let us pray that come it may,
(As come it will for a’ that,)
That Sense and Worth, o’er a’ the earth,
Shall bear the gree, an’ a’ that.
For a’ that, an’ a’ that,
It’s coming yet for a’ that,
That man to man, the warld o’er,
Shall brothers be for a’ that.  @bananasutra lyrics adaptation:  Is there a man who walks with pride,
Though poor and worn, and all that?
The coward bows, but we’ll abide,

The crown is but a stamped disguise,
A man’s a man for all that. What if our table’s plain and bare,
Our coats are thin, and all that?
Let fools delight in silks so rare,
A man’s a man for all that.
For all that and all that,
Their pomp and gold and all that,
An honest heart and mind so free,
Are worth far more than all that. You see that man they call a lord,
Who struts and stares and all that?

(And come it will, for all that,)
When sense and worth, not birth and gold,
Shall lead the world, and all that.
For all that and all that,
It’s coming yet, for all that,
That man to man, both far and wide,
Shall brothers be for all that.

Two sister-songs, with lyrics directly inspired by Dr. Ramani’s video “Narcissism: The Secondhand Smoke of Mental Health” (on YouTube)...  Why “secondhand smoke”? * Even if you don’t have NPD, being around narcissists makes you sick. * The harm spreads outward: family, partners, coworkers absorb the toxicity.   Five recognizable patterns: 1. Malignant/toxic narcissist – sadistic, manipulative, close to psychopathy. 2. Grandiose narcissist – bragging, flashy, entitled. 3. Covert/vulnerable narcissist – “woe is me,” hyper-sensitive, passive-aggressive. 4. Communal narcissist – the #hashtag-do-gooder; public philanthropy, private cruelty. 5. Benign narcissist – vapid, superficial, not as cruel, but emotionally shallow.  Seven diagnostic hallmarks (the “big seven”): 1. Lack of empathy (the bedrock). 2. Entitlement. 3. Grandiosity. 4. Superficiality. 5. Chronic need for admiration/validation. 6. Rage when threatened. 7. Arrogance (dismissiveness, devaluation).  Other patterns: - Gaslighting, projection, exploitation, jealousy, schadenfreude, manipulation. - Comorbidity with depression, substance abuse, compulsive sex/love behaviors. Impact on others: - Creates learned helplessness: partners feel nothing they do makes a difference. - Can devastate self-esteem, health, and careers.  Treatment: - Narcissists rarely seek therapy voluntarily. - Progress is very slow, at best moving them from toxic → tolerable. - No medication cures narcissism. - Empathy must be cultivated early; prevention is everything.  Hopeful note: - Empathy is teachable in children. Parents should model and mirror empathy above all else.  --- SIDE A EPx3: “Secondhand Smoke”   [Intro]
Step right up, darlings, don’t choke, This song is called secondhand smoke.
It’s about cocksure egos. Ha. Ready? Down we go.  [Verse 1]
No mirror inside, so they borrow your face,
Validation’s the drug they chase.
Shiny cars, hollow eyes,
Charm that blinds, and charm that lies.  [Chorus ]
Mirror, mirror, what do you know?
Arrogant hearts all need a glow show.

Entitled thrones on borrowed ground,

Grand illusions, paper crowns,
Lift you up, then tear you down.  [Chorus ]
Mirror, mirror, what do you know?
Arrogant hearts all need a glow show.
Praise me, praise me… but can you grow? Like, can you flow and bow? (Or just blow, blow?)  [Bridge]
No empathy, no remedy,
Woke ain’t like smoke, ain’t your enemy.
Round and round, the blowers spin,
And sorrow seeps through my skin.  [Outro]
Step away, darling, break the spell,
Breathe your own air, and breathe it well.
Leave their circus, let them choke,  On their own secondhand smoke.  --- SIDE B EPx3: "Arrogant hearts"  [Verse 1] Step right up to the mirror maze,
Where charm is cheap and love decays,
They smile so wide while they cut you thin,
Secondhand smoke seeps under your skin.   [Chorus] No empathy, no remedy,
Entitlement is their melody,
Grandiose ghosts on high ego stage,
Arrogant hearts and their puppets cage.   [Verse 2]
Superficial saints with a selfie crown,
Validation junkies shake you down,
Malice erupts when masks won’t stay,
Gaslight fever keeps truth at bay.   [Bridge]
“Ladies and gents, beware the show!
They’ll promise excellence, deliver shadow.
Communal halos, malignant schemes,
Covert whispers, grandiose dreams!”  [Final Chorus] Learned helplessness in smoky air,
You breathe their poison unaware,
The crowd applauds, the tyrant grins,
But emptiness echoes where soul cannot sing.

_desc-yt: “Blessed are the cracked” is a modern proverb and folk wisdom sometimes (falsely) attributed to Groucho Marx—an aphorism that plays off the biblical “Beatitudes” style, with a poetic twist. It has circulated widely in motivational and spiritual circles, sometimes altered to: “There is a crack in everything, that’s how the light gets in,” which is a verifiable line from Leonard Cohen’s song “Anthem.”   The bananasutra lyrics are generally about embracing imperfection, humor, and the cracks that let the light in… and is specifically inspired by the following quotes from Bertrand Russel—one of my all-time fav imaginary down-under boyfriends (ha):  “People's opinions are mainly designed to make them feel comfortable; truth, for most people, is a secondary consideration.” “Most people would sooner die than think; in fact, they do.” “War does not determine who is right—only who is left.” “It is preoccupation with possessions, more than anything else, that prevents us from living freely and nobly.” “The only thing that will redeem mankind is cooperation.” “The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge.” “To be without some of the things you want is an indispensable part of happiness.” “The secret of happiness is this: let your interests be as wide as possible, and let your reactions to the things and persons that interest you be as far as possible friendly rather than hostile.” “A sense of duty is useful in work, but offensive in personal relations. People wish to be liked, not to be endured.” “The world is full of magical things patiently waiting for our wits to grow sharper.”  (Verse 1) Blessed are the cracked, the broken, the bruised, The ones who laugh though life’s been unkind, For every scar’s a map, every crack’s a muse, And through the gaps, the light unwinds.  (Chorus) Blessed are the cracked, for they shall shine, Through the fractures of this fragile design. A little offbeat, a little askew, Blessed are the cracked, just like you.  (Verse 2) Oh, perfect is a prison, a gilded lie, Where laughter dies and hearts grow cold. But in the cracked, the crooked, the wry, Is a warmth that’s worth more than gold.  (Chorus) Blessed are the cracked, for they shall shine, Through the fractures of this fragile design. A little offbeat, a little askew, Blessed are the cracked, just like you.  (Bridge) Let’s drink to the fools, the clumsy, the lost, Who stumble but never resign. For in every tumble, in every cost, Is a wisdom that grows with time.  (Outro) So laugh with the cracks, let the light pour through, Blessed are the broken—blessed are you. A little offbeat, a little askew, Blessed are the cracked, just like you.

You’d think it wouldn’t take a media exec or growth wizard to grasp a few simple truths:  1. Competing with Spotify, Apple, or TikTok? You need to invest in emerging artists.  2. Most of us don’t have the time, money, or energy to make multiple-format videos.  3. Vertical is the standard. It’s what mobile-native, youth-heavy audiences expect.  4. Good songs are often longer than 3 minutes. The new Shorts limit is a mismatch.  5. Real music lovers—creators and listeners—don’t vibe with arbitrary corporate constraints.  So… why is YouTube’s music growth strategy still so clunky? As a nerdy music fan and digital strategist, it baffles me. Like, how is this not obvious?  Bottom banana: If YouTube wants to be taken seriously as a music platform, it needs to give Music its own dedicated Shorts format—and show it actually cares about artists and audiences.  Take it from a win-win strategist: Build community, not just compliance. The payoff is real.  And hey, if you made it this far, congrats—you’re officially part of the 0.001% with heart, soul and curiosity.  #musicheals #vocaljazz #sunomusic #aivoice #YouTubeMusic #ShortsTooShort

_desc-sc: “Everybody is genius. But if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing it is stupid.”—Albert Einstein   One thing I believe is that children hold more genius than we let them be! This song is a thank you to Albert, and also a love song for ‘em kids—kinda like a lullaby I would sing to my child, if I had one… because growing up in a world gone bananas sure ain’t easy!  Also, fun nerd fact: Math never came easy to me, but I always felt it was a form of language that can help explain things words cannot, kinda like poetry… and—it just recently recently occurred to me— my favorite humanists are all genius mathematicians 🥸 there’s Albert, whose wisdom of the heart was just as great as his earthly physics contributions, and then, there’s Blaise (Pascal), and Bertrand (Russel). I’ll be praying they form a post-punk band in heaven called “my dead genius boyfriends” 🤘  — Genius, you see, If you judge a fish by climbing trees, It won’t be free, It’s true, it’s true, so don’t you doubt your mind, You’re one of a kind, And I hope you find, Your worth inside.  In life, we all see, That there’s a way we’re meant to be, But don’t agree, With the rules they set for you, ‘cause you’re, More than they know, Just let it show, You’ll find your glow.  (Chorus) Don’t feel small, don’t feel small, don’t feel small, You’ve got it all inside, Your wings just need to fly. They’ll see it too, see it too, see it too, Once you believe it’s true, That genius lives in you.  They’ll try to say, You should fit into their way, But don’t obey, You’ve got gifts they cannot see, and so, Let yourself shine, Don’t stay behind, You’ll change their mind.  (Chorus) Don’t feel small, don’t feel small, don’t feel small, You’ve got it all inside, Your wings just need to fly. They’ll see it too, see it too, see it too, Once you believe it’s true, That genius lives in you.  Genius, you see, If you judge a fish by climbing trees, It won’t be free, But you’re meant to be, just as you are, Shine like a star, You’ll go so far, ‘Cause you’re a work of art.

Because Gladys is my middle name, and "Sonder" is a magic feeling of knowing wonder--when each stranger you see is the main character of their own life, and you are merely an extra in their story... The word was coined by author John Koenig and first appeared in "The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows", a project that creates names for emotions that don't have one  🕳️🐇   Gipsy Burlesque Blues Dream @bananasutra EPx14 #lyrics (variations):  [Intro – Down the Rabbit Dream]  The curtain breathes smoke, the dream’s out of tune, Gladys sings sideways beneath the fool moon. Mister White Rabbit spins clocks out of thin sand, time melts in mirrors all over the land. The Chessshire Cat strips in a glitch ’n bitch show, Whispering, “Truth’s just a pathetic trick, meow.” And Gladys keeps falling, big heart in her hand, into the bassline bloom of Sonderland.   [Chorus 1 – The Dance of Sonder]  Gladys in Sonderland, dance out of line, chase that White Rabbit with a glass of wine. Truth traded by cocky kings and sons, Love is fool, woke… screw their whacky plans. Oh laugh, my loves, the joke’s still grand, we all fall slow in Sonderland.  [Bridge – The Burlesque of Empathy]  Contempt kills the courage meant to soothe, Fear builds a cage on a stage, proof. The Cat draws claws in nonsense sand, the Queen flips hearts like contraband. And Sonder sighs, and Gladys sings with the band: Love that sees, not love that blinds, unchains the demons from our minds.  [Final Chorus – The Carnival Crescendo] Gladys in Sonderland, lift up your mask, toast to the fools who dare to ask. White Rabbit’s gone, the clocks are banned, we measure love by gone grains of sand. So laugh, my loves, the truth’s divine, the heart’s a door, swing open wide. Gladys in Sonderland, you understand: we fall to rise, we blend to mend.  [Outro – The Curtain Closes, or Maybe Opens] The Queen wipes the blood from her wonder lips. The Cat hums an old stolen hymn, its grin dissolving from outside to in. Gladys stands amazed, champagne in her hand, and bows to the holes of Sonderland. She laughs… It’s absurd, but it’s hers, this plan, to lose herself just to understand… “Every fall’s a beginning; Blessed be holes, Son.”   🥂 🎶
_desc-yt: “Gladys in Sonderland” is a wonder #waltz rewrite of an existential bananasutra song originally titled “Alice and the order of love”… a humanist, empathetic reflection about modern society, which more or less mirrored mirror the great #jacquesbrel song “Quand on a que l’amour”.   And, in case you’re curious (like me), “Gladys” is meaningfool (to me) because it is my real middle name (a true wonder, for a 100% French girl;), and “Sonder” is a magick word meant to express the realization that everyone has a lens of life as personal, deep, and complex as your own…  —⁠ @bananasutra #songlyrics   [Intro : Waltz] The curtain was velvet, the moon a disguise,and Gladys stepped through where the looking glass lies.The floorboards were breathing, the clocks out of hand,and down she kept falling through Sonderland. They warned her of faith, they warned her of sin,and mocked the light that burned within.So gather, my darlings, the brave and the damned,to hear what she found in Sonderland.  [Verse 1 : The Idol of Romance] They built their thrones from pain,and crowned their teeth with gain.They swore that great was bright,then stole the people’s light.But hubris blinds the wise,it’s foolish still to pray,to idols made of sighs,those who steal souls away.  [Chorus] Oh Gladys in Sonderland, look what we’ve done,we sold our hearts to everyone.We trade our grace for borrowed trust,we kiss the gold and call it just.But love that sees, not love that shines,can free the ghosts inside our minds. _desc-sc: “Hello, Oh No?” is a silly, cheeky GROWsutra true story that sings like psychedelic poetry, a hope-fool tune asking simple questions that actually matter, in a world gone mad bananas, a world that forgot how cute it is to blush... Think of it as a friendly wink in the dark, a small song with big questions—playful on the surface, philosophical underneath.  It’s about the magic healing power of free will, the importance of critical thinking with a pulse. It’s about courage, honesty, humility, and unity, i.e. the superpowers we misplaced somewhere on the cha-ching media conveyor belt, where noise dressed up as wisdom, and ego bought a throne and called it strength—because really, who(tf) sold us the myth that success means crushing others, and fear beats love? And why(tf) did we applaud?!  I wrote this for the brave dreamers and future-makers, to dare you to care for the kids and the grown-ups who got bamboozled along the way; the ones who were told empathy was weak and win-win was naïve, while hollow peacocks in blinged-out power suits paraded around calling hoarding “leadership.” Even though history keeps whispering the same truth: it is kindness that defines real winners.  This song hums a gentle but stubborn reminder: real winners don’t blindfold themselves for comfort. They choose spark over dark. Win-win over win-lose that end up being lose-lose. Empathy over hypocrisy. Unity over vanity. Because, see... kindness isn’t weakness, it’s clarity. Win-win isn’t cute or “woke”, it’s pragamatic, it's empiric, it's strategic. And humility? Oh darling, that’s DIVINE!  And maybe, just maybe, if we stop mistaking leadership for expensive cosplay, and start choosing clearer hearts over louder heroes, maybe we’ll see through the toxic smoke of shiny mirrors? Maybe we’ll recognize ego-madness when it struts by, cocky dressed as fancy progress. Maybe we’ll even learn (or remember) to laugh at (not with) the pompous Prometheus and snake oil fraudsters,  selling cha-ching over win-win sharing… Maybe. Can we?  So now, hello, oh no?!… What will you choose, bro? The choice is (y)ours. Facts matter and the reality is that people's opinions prioritize comfort over truth, and personal values and principles do vary widely based on their individual experiences, cultural backgrounds, upbringing, and personal philosophies, i.e. their conscious and unconscious fears... Another song for our Public Domain Revolution inspiration collection, and my tribute to Victor Hugo’s French revolutionary spirit—its poignant poetry, and adamant urgency…  (In)Famous lines (translated from French):
"And, standing proud, my soul shall tell / The tyrants of the earth—farewell!"   Original French Text: Liberté (1821) – Victor Hugo  Gloire à toi, Liberté! toi dont le temple immense
Est bâti dans les cieux sur l'éternelle loi!
L'homme est fait pour ton culte, et dans son cœur immense
Tu dois régner comme un dieu-roi. Gloire à toi! Déjà l'ombre a fui devant l'aurore,
Déjà sous d'autres cieux l'éclair luit,
Et l'avenir, couvert de lumière sonore,
Sort du tombeau de cette nuit. Levez-vous! peuples nus, esclaves des despotes!
Brisez vos fers! le jour est pur!
Peuples! à vos bourreaux, à leurs lois scélérates
Opposez la justice et l'azur! Que votre front s'éclaire aux feux de la tempête!
Que l’orage ouvre enfin vos yeux!
Que dans le grand combat, sous la foudre honnête,
Votre cri soit juste et glorieux! Ah! que vois-je? Ils se lèvent! ô sublime armée!
Debout sous l'étendard vivant!
Et moi, debout aussi, mon âme enflammée
Dira: aux tyrans de la terre—adieu!  @bananasutra lyrics, i.e. my poetic English translation, channeling Bob, for the People:)  Liberty  Glory to you, O Liberty!—your boundless temple
Rises in the heavens, built on eternal law!
Man was made to serve you, and in his mighty heart
You must reign as a god, in awe. Glory to you!—Already the shadows flee the sunrise,
Already under distant skies the lightning glows,
And the future, crowned with roaring light,
Rises from the grave where darkness grows. Rise up, ye naked peoples—slaves of tyrant masters!
Break your chains! The day is bright!
People! To your butchers, to their wicked laws,
Oppose but justice and the sky’s clear light! Let the storm’s fire ignite your brow with fury!
Let the tempest open your eyes at last!
That in this righteous battle, beneath honest thunder,
Your cry be noble, fierce, and vast! Ah!—What do I see? They rise!—O sublime army!
They stand beneath the living flag once more!
And I, standing proud, my soul aflame,
Shall tell the tyrants of the earth—farewell forevermore!

Lyrics inspired by Bertrand Russel's "Marriage and Morals", where he asked: "Are prostitution and traditional marriage interconnected by hypocritical societal structures and discriminatory economic dependency?"   In this long essay/book, Bertrand fairly observes that marriage often prioritizes financial stability and social status over love, mirroring prostitution’s very transactional nature, and  critiques the rigidity of marital norms, such as lifelong exclusivity and fidelity, arguing it often stifle desires, and lead to unmet physical, emotional, and spiritual needs.  He makes bold statements: “Marriage is for women the commonest mode of livelihood, and the total amount of undesired sex endured by women is probably greater in marriage than in prostitution.”   And asks brave questions: “What if pr0stituti0n was required as a societal “release valve” for repressed desires, existing mostly as the condemned counterpart to marriage?”  But(t) his point really is this: Why not think of marriage as a relationship based on equality, respect, and personal freedom, i.e. friendship? Could practicing truth, and trust, with humility and integrity, help reduce foul plays--including society’s reliance on femmes de joie, for example, heh?   Well duh, d'oh, heck yeah!? And… if you're doubting the veracity and value of Bertrand's kind and wise questions and observations, here's a fun fact for ya: marital r⭐︎pe was A-OK legal in almost ALL countries of the world, until the mid-90s?! _desc-sc: “Rage bait” was named the 2025 Word of the Year by the Oxford dictionary, and frankly, it’s no surprise. We are witnessing a grotesque circus of injustice—a global crisis that leaves many of us feeling powerless against the cold, cruel gears of the so-called new world order. And I, for one, often find myself holding my breath, standing at the edge of an increasingly scary, angry, insane lose-lose reality…  I wrote “One Percent Rising” almost a year ago, as a sort of torch song for the Curious, the Honest, and the Unseen. Inspired by a deep-dive personality test that placed me in "the top 1% of Curiosity", this song is a reminder of how rare and vital Universalism, Humility, and Authenticity have become; how much they matter, in a world that feels like a deadly toxic "hog-feed" of manufactured noise, led by "suits and ties" high on ego, fear, and conformity. It’s meant to be like a spark in the fog, for me, and for you, and everyone, equally… if you dare to care ;) Think of it as a lill’ pep talk, a friendly 'n fresh breath of hope, to feed sensitive and sensible souls—a prayer of sorts, for Creative (r)Evolution.   With this song, I want to encourage prioritizing curiosity over competition, and sincerity over status, to help us feel like we can rise above this fasc!st tsunami... while others brainlessly and heartlessly admire and rewards nefarious ”Power Hoarders", like a herd of ignorant "Conformity Bros”, aka sheeples... Because, in an era gone fool on backward bananas—where global fascist trends and dehumanizing antics posture as “smart”, glorifying deceit in the name of greed—what we need, to solve dire problems, to survive, essentially, is a hell of a lot of imagination, rooted in altruism. I believe that with all my KNOWing and BLOWing guts!  And so here I go again, reimagining the French ideals of "liberté, égalité, fraternité", through my candid, psychedelic lens, and praying for the good kind of “weird” to rise—not through force, but(t) through the "sharp perfume" of curiosity, in the name of truth seeking, enlightenment through knowledge and transparency... i.e. what it would actually take to help make the world a better-not-worse place, for 99% of us.   Blessed be the sincere, brave, creative outliers who refuse to stop GROWing, those who can fathom how to keep blooming in a mad, hostile world! Oh and, “thank god for dogs”, you know? ;)  — EPx6 flows from Psychedelic Punk Rock (1-3) to Gipsy LOFI (4-6). It's raw, imperfect, and radically hope fool... _desc-sc: DEFY is a soul-deep, whispered scream BLOWsutra EP in 7 Tracks, which started with one question: “What are we doing?”  That’s the question @defiance13 asked in a heartfelt #TikTok monologue that cracked something in me. He was not being not rhetorical—he was being real. Caring. Conscious. Raw. Clear. Bright. Informed. Logical. Ethical. Philosophical. Outraged. Defiant. And I weeped, silently, in empathy. He sounded like Hope, with a capital H, like, just Human.  This EP is what came out of sitting with that question. Not answers, but grief. Not slogans, but songs.Three core truths, seven different renderings of them—raw and low, no sweetening. Just me, my conscience, and my lyrics. Because lyrics matter. Because denial is poison. It names names, connects dots, quotes sources, maps connections, and asks: when did control become our national art form? When did cruelty become a campaign style?  And the third [track 6-7], “Universal Currency,” is the hardest to sing. It’s a quiet scream for the children—those who die in floods, in heat, in systems designed to forget them. It’s about how this country penciled out the price of a child’s life—just under $109,000—and still dared to call it justice. But children are not budget lines. They’re our only true wealth. And the exchange rate is human decency.  Each version of these songs brings out a slightly different truth—one more bluesy, one more folk, one more hypnotic or theatrical. They’re not remixes. They’re re-feelings. This is not background music. It’s not a brand. It’s basically just my gut’s voice... And if you're wondering too, what (TF) are we doing, then maybe these songs are for you too. Because defiance, when nothing else is left, is love’s last language.  ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰ ✰   Lyrics gladly shared upon request.

_desc-sc: Light me up, librarian lover… and "Read Me Harder" EPX19 📚💨 Side A x9 = Gypsy HopFi Fusion BURLESQUE Edition Side B x10 = Psychedelic Americana BLUES Edition  I was listening to my "S.S. is for Sacred Sp3rm" EP when I saw yet another one of those daily terrifying #breakingnews social media posts, listing #books recently #banned from the (remaining) U.S. Public Schools and Libraries #circa2025  1. The Handmaid’s Tale by Margaret Atwood 2. Brave New World, by Aldous Huxley 3. Fahrenheit 451 by Ray Bradbury 4. 1984 by George Orwell 5. To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee 6. The perks of being a wallflower, by Stephen Chbovsky 7. The Bluest Eye by Toni Morrison  8. Sold by Patricia McCormick 9. Maus by Art Spiegelman 10. An African and Latinx History of the United States by Paul Ortiz  So then, I had to write a "B.B. is for BANNED BOOKS" song, to honor my favorite authors on this list, because WOW... HOW freaking SCARY of an #americanhorror #truestory IS THAT?!   ☆☆☆ @bananasutra lyrics:  [Intro] They banned the truth for being rude… But baby, rude is how we bloom. So light me up, librarian lover… and read me harder. B.B. is for Banned Books, and Badass Brains.  [Verse 1 – Harper Lee & Art Spiegelman] Harper told me, “Mock me, kill me,” still I sing, Truth’s a mockingbird with wings. Art drew the pain, a mouse in flame, He said, “Remember, never tame.” You can ban my ink, but not my roar, I’ll scratch your walls, and write some more.  [Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! If thinking’s sin, I’ll take the blame, Desire and truth are one and same.  [Verse 2 – Aldous Huxley & Margaret Atwood] Aldous whispered, “Take your soma, stay asleep,” But sugar, freedom don’t come cheap. Atwood smirked, “Blessed be the fruit,” Then laced her boots and staged a coup. Pop your soma, hush your fear, But holy lust still lights us clear.  [Bridge – George Orwell & Ray Bradbury] Big Brother’s watching, Ray lit the spark, Said, “Burn the dark, not those who mark.” Orwell winked through smoke and steam, “Truth’s a thoughtcrime, love’s the dream.” You can’t delete what won’t forget, We’re the match they can’t reset.  [Final Chorus] They banned the books but not the beat, Banned the thought but not the heat, Banned the love but not the street. So read me, baby, read me sweet! Truth’s taboo, but damn, it’s neat, Come turn the page with me.  [Outro] For Harper Lee, Art Spiegelman, Aldous Huxley, Margaret Atwood, George Orwell, and Ray Bradbury, for every mind they tried to muzzle. We see you. We feel you. And we’ll keep reading you harder.

His essay aims to answer a question I've asked myself for as long as I can remember, an important one: “Has Religion Contributed Anything Useful to Civilization?”   His answer? This song echoes that spirit: a love letter to curiosity, courage, and clarity. _desc-yt: “Where Wonder Lies” is a sister song of “Question Di Kingdom”, and initially titled “Reason over Reverence”.   The lyrics are inspired by my sweetheart mathematician philosopher #bertrandrussell and his 1929 essay on Religion, where he asks a fair question: “has religion contributed anything good to society?”…  Bertrand Russell critiques the historical and contemporary role of religion in society. His main points include:  1. Positive Contributions Are Not Unique to Religion:  While acknowledging some moral and cultural contributions by religious figures and institutions, Russell argues these are not exclusive to religion. Secular philosophy, science, and humanism have made equivalent or greater contributions without relying on dogma.  2. Obstacles to Progress:  Russell highlights religion’s frequent opposition to scientific progress, intellectual freedom, and social reform. He critiques its role in fostering intolerance, wars, and dogmatic thinking.  3. Ethical Limitations:  According to Russell, religious morality often enforces outdated and harmful principles, rooted in obedience to authority rather than rational compassion.  4. Human Potential Without Religion:  He asserts that humanity can achieve moral progress and meaning through reason, science, and humanistic values, without needing supernatural beliefs.  Russell concludes that while religion has occasionally contributed to civilization, it has more often been an impediment to critical thinking, freedom, and progress…  I once read songwriters end up writing the same songs over and over…. And this all means so much to me, I get it now—most of my songs lyrics explore these very themes; this essay alone inspired several songs (or stories, as I like to think of it)! Et pendant ce temps… on recule (pour ne pas dire on se fait encouler ha;)  Cette chanson parle des mots sont retournés, des crimes maquillés en vertu, et du monde qui glisse, lentement mais sûrement, vers une version aussi ringarde que cruelle et dangereuse: un nouveau vieux monde plus autoritaire, plus religieux, plus militarisé, plus masculin, dans le pire sens du terme—un monde ou l’art de la domination au nom du contrôle rend la violence (physique et psychologique) “légitime”.  Un “secret de Polichinelle”, en français, c’est une expression commune pour décrire une vérité que tout le monde connaît, mais que tout le monde fait semblant d’ignorer... C’est le mensonge collectif confortable. C’est le roi nu qu’on continue d’applaudir. C’est le cirque qui tourne pendant que la maison brûle.  Le secret de Polichinelle du jour, c’est que le monde régresse vers une forme d’impérialisme viriliste, fascisant, dogmatique, emballé en “ordre”, “valeurs”, “protection”, “foi”, “tradition”, “bon sens”…  On dit “paix” pour vendre des bombes. On dit “Dieu” pour justifier les maîtres. On dit “ordre” pour exiger l’obéissance. On dit “amour” pour faire avaler la violence…  Bananasutra, c’est l’art de dire les verités d’un monde complètement bananes, de rire pendant qu’on panique, de danser pendant que tout semble s’éffondrer. C’est de la satire tendre et cruelle à la fois... un cabaret politique pour temps de fin de cycle.  Si ça te fait rire → bien. Si ça te met mal à l’aise → encore mieux. Si ça te donne envie de questionner, désobéir, crier, et créer, pour le droit d’aimer vraiment, librement → bingo 🍌  ⸻  #inenglish   “Secret de Polichinelle” literally means “an open (absurd) secret.” It’s something everybody knows, but nobody dares say. And while nobody says it… freaking things slide backwards.  This song is about that surreal moment when words are but(t) excuses, crimes are rebranded as virtues, and the world quietly drifts toward a naughty retro version of itself: more authoritarian, more religious, more militarized, more male-dominated—in for the sheer sake of domination, hierarchy, control, and “legitimate” violence.  A “secret de Polichinelle” is a collective lie of convenience. For example, the naked king we keep applauding... The absurdity of the circus clowns who keep farting while the house is on fire.  Here, the “open secret” is this: That we are sliding into a new form of imperial, masculinist, fascistic regression, but we package it as “order,” “values,” “protection,” “faith,” “tradition,” or “common sense.” Sigh.  We say “peace” to sell bombs. We say “God” to justify masters. We say “order” to demand obedience. We say “love” to make violence swallowable…  Bananasutra is the art of telling truths that matter in a world gone rotten bananas—laughing while panicking, dancing while dismantling the set… Tender and cruel satire for end-of-cycle times. _desc-yt: Like all @bananasutra songs, this is not just a song; it’s a story I often tell myself, and care to share—inspired by Carl Sagan, and my GROWsutra philosophy.   The lyrics are rooted in one of Carl Sagan’s most haunting insights: “One of the saddest lessons of history is this: If we’ve been bamboozled long enough, we tend to reject any evidence of the bamboozle. We’re no longer interested in finding the truth. The bamboozle has captured us. It’s simply too painful to acknowledge (even to ourselves) that we’ve been taken. Once you give a charlatan power over you, you almost never get it back.”  It’s a story rooted in the GROWsutra spirit: a philosophy of fierce compassion, where curiosity is stronger than comfort, where questioning is a form of kindness, and where truth, though sometimes bitter, is ultimately the beginning of healing.  This track’s rhythm mirrors the lyrical flow of Morrissey’s “Some Girls Are Bigger Than Others” song, rewritten into “Some Truths Are Harder to Swallow”—as a smooth but subversive protest lullaby. It feels like a velvet revolt in slow motion, a mellow jazz noir meditation on denial, pride, memory, and the painful beauty of waking up…  My good friend the octopus also makes a quiet appearance here too—as a symbol of memory, intelligence, adaptability, and mystery. Because the real revolution will not be televised. It will be sensed, remembered, grown into. It will happen quietly, in places where eyes are open and minds remain unbought… because, in an authoritarian society, one thing is for sure: revolution ain’t gonna be televised! KNOWsutra : Prometheus ➵ Gave fire (knowledge) to humans; punished for empowering truth. A true win-win rebel. 2. BLOWsutra : Hydra + Medusa ➵ Hydra: corrupt systems that grow stronger when attacked wrong. Medusa: demonized femininity + misunderstood power. 3. SHOWsutra : Dionysus ➵ God of ecstatic joy, chaos, music, and theatre. Shows the sacred side of silliness and subversion. 4. FLOWsutra : Hermes ➵ Trickster god of transitions, language, and messages. A master of in-betweenness. 5. GROWsutra : Persephone ➵ Her cycle (abduction and return) teaches growth through descent and rebirth. Feminine resilience myth. 6. GLOWsutra : Apollo + Hestia ➵ Apollo = light, art, and healing. Hestia = the hearth, peace, inner warmth. 7. BOWsutra : Orpheus ➵ Music so beautiful it moved the gods. Journeyed to the underworld for love—faith, failure, and awe.  ♆♆♆ @bananasutra #lyrics   [Verse 1 – KNOW : Prometheus] Every truth you KNOW   Flickers soft and low   Like a stolen flame   From a god of shame   He gave us fire, paid the toll   To free the know from control    [Verse 2 – BLOW / Hydra + Medusa] Every cruel BLOW   Feeds the beast below   Cut one head, three rise   In the name of lies   And still we cage her rage and grace   To fear what dares to blow this place    [Verse 3 – SHOW : Dionysus ] Every mask you SHOW   Hides the pain you stow   But the sacred jest   Is a truth confessed   He laughs through wounds the wise won’t see   To show what dares to set us free    [Verse 4 – GROW : Persephone] Every time you GROW   You descend below   Like the seeds she sows   Where the silence knows   That roots need dark to rise again   And grow through loss, not just through gain    [Verse 5 – FLOW : Hermes ] Every word you FLOW   Is a place you go   Past the borderlines   Of the gods' designs   Hermes walks where logic ends   To let new meanings flow through bends    [Verse 6 – GLOW : Apollo + Hestia ] Every time you GLOW   Through the ache and slow   You become the spark   In the temple dark   He sings the wounds she warms to heal   They glow in silence, soft and real    [Verse 7 – BOW : Orpheus ] Every time you BOW   To the here and now   Like Orpheus did   For the love he hid   You trust the gods to give it back   But some truths die when we bow to lack    [Outro] Synthema… Sutra…   We know… we blow…   We show… we grow…   We flow… we glow…   And sometimes… we bow…    ♆♆♆

The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill.
And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.
 2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.
 3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.
 4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.
 5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.
 6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.
 2. Affection: Love given and love received.
 3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.
 4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.
 5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.
 6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).
 7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

_desc-sc: "The Great Naked King" is a SHOWsutra song about the oldest trick in the book: convince the crowd that what they cannot see is proof of their own unworthiness. The song borrows its title from Chaplin's 1940 masterpiece "The Great Dictator"—the most tender act of political foolishness in cinema history. They both understood that laughter is not the opposite of seriousness. It is what seriousness becomes when it has nothing left to lose.  So here we are. Laughing. On purpose. At the pageantry, the bling-bling, the paper crowns, the hollow halls, the crooked applause, the vast collective hallucination stitched together in pompous complicity and called a nation... Until, somewhere in the crowd, a brave small voice (who knows better) speaks up. Simple truth with humble poise. _desc-yt: 00:00 - “Invisible Man in the Sky” Track 1 03:17 - “Invisible Man in the Sky” Track 2  Blessed be George Carlin, and all the brave bringers of truth, light, and laughter.  His razor-sharp awareness of the absurd is a precious gift—not to say a real blessing, ha. This song is part of the GROWsutra (God, Etc) bananasutra collection, and directly inspired by one of his skits with the same title.  In this skit, George points out how some dubious pundits somehow convinced millions that there’s an invisible man living in the sky, watching everything you do, every minute of every day. He’s got a long list of things he doesn’t want you to do. And if you break the rules? Eternal fire torture. Burning. Screaming. Forever. But don’t worry. He loves you, really. But he also needs your money! Ahem. Oh and, he expects you to confess all your “dirty secrets” to single (and maybe horny) holy man in a dark robe, in a tiny dark room, regularly and unconditionally… so you might be “saved”, in the end. Maybe. True story. Sigh.  God knows I’ve got a whole backlog of songs (mostly questions) about religion. I was raised secular, in a country shaped by separating church and state, and by an authoritarian atheist father who believed religion mostly harmed society. So far, based on lived experience, I get where he was coming from… That said: I do believe there’s real wisdom out there. And Hope matters. Meaning matters.  What breaks my heart is the absurd irony: how curiosity gets hijacked into control. How fear gets packaged as faith. How this story keeps looping… again and again. And I can’t help wondering: Is it ignorance?  Is it insecurity?  Is it power? Is it Evil? And, why, goddamn?! Jesus Christ, wtf, whyyy 😵‍💫  Anyway… Praised be critical thinkers, conscious prayers, George’s sense of humor, and the magic of music! #amen  —  @bananasutra   Lyrics + #AIvoice on #sunomusic 🎧  “Invisible Man in the Sky”  They say there’s someone up above,   An invisible man who means but(t) love,   Judges your life, and keeps a score…   Don’t cross his line, you’ll burn for sure.  He’s got a list, oh, don’t you know?   The things he hates, the sins that blow…   If you don’t obey, you’ll fry and scream,   But he loves you, huh, so it seems. Invisible man in the sky,   Wants your money, makes you cry.   He loves you, oh, it’s true,   But he’ll burn you if you’re through.   Invisible man… invisible man…   In the sky… in the sky…  🖤

"(I Wanted to Be a) Poem" is an experimental jazzy psychedelic song I wrote around the quote “I thought I wanted to be a poet but basically, I wanted to be the poem”; it is lyrically structured after the song “Summertime”, and directly inspired by the following essay about Jaime Gil de Biedma—an introverted, humble poet who lived under the Franco dictatorship, during the Spanish Inquisition (early last century)…  - “Perhaps poetry is best minted under pressure. Poetry that lasts. (...)  Jaime Gil de Biedma lived under Franco. Born in 1929 in Barcelona, Biedma was six when Federico Garcia Lorca was killed by Franco’s troops in Granada. Famously, the story goes that as they shot Lorca his murderers said: “Three shots in the ass for Garcia Lorca for being a faggot.” His body was never found. (…)  Silence carves these poems. He wrote his poems under a dictator who was famous for saying, “You are master of what you don’t say.” Maybe all poems are carved by silence. Think Dickinson. Think Hopkins. Silence can equal life. Here silence is particularly historic in a way it no longer is. Franco shut Spain up. The ground rich with unidentified corpses. Homosexuality denied in a regime that aligned itself with the conservative Catholic Church.  But poetry. Poetry provides a passport to transcendence when pressures seem unsurmountable: and more than thrice a poetry created under pressure in silence trumps death.  As Biedma began to put pen to paper, what preceded him was daunting. All the major poets had vanished: Machado on a death march, Lorca shot, Hernandez dead in prison, Cernuda fled to Mexico and never returned. Decades rolled on, censorship reigned, and torpid inertia smothered art. (...)  Poetry remains indestructible. Poetry outlasts Franco and AIDS. So long as men and women can breathe museums will preserve artifacts and a poet like Biedma will add to the record of what life was like under oppression.”

It is why we choose to join the dance, why we break into a trance, why we find balance, why we care to dare bare the lore of lies untold. Truth is the soul that fuels the bold, the brave, it is the fire that burns in one’s true heart’s desire, the only prayer that shines like it’s divine. Truth is the beat of intimate intentions, the pulse of our deepest motivations, the seed of true  salvation. The truth is the only truth that matters is raw, it’s the reason WHY we love to share, WHY we dare to be in the bare, WHY we hope to win, why we pray we live. Because there’s no prayer like desire." _desc-sc: This 5-track GLOWsutra EP is a loving tribute to Lucille Clifton’s iconic poem “What the Mirror Said.”, en Français. It's like a bouquet arrangement of spoken word and minimal jazz celebrating clarity, grace, and unapologetic feminine truth. Rather than reinterpret the poem, I respond to it—in my native language... mirroring its message in sound, with subtle keys, hushed harmonies, and soul-deep phrasing, finding radiance in my shadows.  GLOWsutra is the chapter of BananaSutra dedicated to gratitude, grace, and the brilliance of being, and this EP a quiet celebration of all who remember who they are.  -- @bananasutra lyrics:   [Verse 1] C’est vrai, Tu sais ? On est tous des p’tites merveilles, Des âmes perdues, mais sans pareil.  En fait, On a tous des cartes en soi, Des trésors que personne ne voit.  [Pre-Chorus] Une histoire de femme dévouée, Une boussole pour mieux se trouver. Une chanson pour aller danser, Un humour discret, mais prêt à briller.  Toujours prête à rigoler, Pour effacer le mystère à oublier. T’es un feu, un fleuve, une immensité, Un éclat que personne ne peut dompter.  [Chorus] Écoute bien, Même au loin, Reste lucide, (Envole-toi) dans le vide.  Ne joue pas la pose, laisse éclater ta voix. Un homme qui pose ses mains sur toi Touche une reine, un trésor, une foi. Dis-leur bien, femme géographie : Ils se perdront sans ta lumière, ta vie.

I considered making the 1000th track special, but I’m not that special, really ;)  This is Vol. 02 of a song I love, “How do Kids Learn Now?” aka “When did seduction become so Untrue?”, a sonic question mark wrapped in 16-track Flamenco Techno journey made of lit Gipsy soul, Arabesk minimalism, flamenco fire, and wonder… asking: What are we teaching? _desc-sc:
This is a GROWsutra (Kindness) song that started as a comment on a meme about “Idiot Compassion”. It is dedicated to people who believe empathy is essentially a “performative” thing… simply because they can’t feel any, but(t) for themselves.
  🌼 🌼 🌼 My original comment:  But who are the idiots lacking mindfulness really? The ones who care to ask, imagine, and relate, in an attempt to understand? Or, the ones who mock or shame them?  What I've observed is that those who frame compassion as manipulative also seem unable to imagine a version of compassion that isn’t about dominance... And that, to me, very much feels like cynical projection. Arguing that putting yourself in someone else’s shoes is essentially self-serving and deluded is very much a narcissistic worldview, a dark, flawed projection, by someone who simply, sadly cannot empathize.  In my divine book of joyful wisdom, what’s idiotic (and weak, and dangerous even) is interpreting curiosity, humility, openness, and tenderness as an hypocritical / tactical power exchange move motivated by a need for control, rather than a desire to connect and understand. Healthy empathy requires both mindfulness and imagination. And, I feel strongly that compassion is (by far) humanity's best line of defense against the global rise of fascism.  Real compassion ain’t dumb, it is brave. And it’s the best goddamn weapon the people got, to lead a peace rebellion.   🌼 🌼 🌼 And, the @bananasutra #songlyrics it became:  [Verse 1] Please tell me, my dear, who’s the fool in this affair? The one leaning in closer just to truly hear?  The one taking time to decode someone’s pain? Or the one throwing shade ’cause the truth bends their frame?  Who hides from the mirror, dodging their own glare? Who calls love “a weakness” ’cause they’re naked under there?  [Pre-Chorus] There’s a chant on the timeline: “Empathy is weak,” they speak, like compassion’s some disaster that’ll crack them in a week.  But if your own reflection cuts too sharp to stare, you call honesty a trap and torch what you can’t repair.  [Chorus] Real compassion isn’t frail, it illuminates the night. Not a failure, not a fairytale, just the discipline of light.  It’s the strength to stay steady when a story starts to tear; no pretending, no performance, just the quiet will to care.  [Verse 2] Funny how the cynics swear that tenderness is “bait,” a ploy, a polished tactic, some seductive sugar-gate.  But hearts afraid of contact fear the feelings they can’t feel, so they label trust “delusion” ’cause they doubt that love is real.  Ask them softly, Bananasutra: “Is it truth you fear… or proof?” Watch the armor split and shimmer like an old forgotten youth.  [Pre-Chorus] They say open hearts will “break you,” curiosity will “fail,” mindful listening is “naïve,” warmth is “cheap and just for sale.”  But a lie screamed repeatedly starts dressing up as “true,” ’til the echo chambers tremble ’cause they’ve drowned out something new.  [Chorus] Real compassion has a spine soft enough for fears to land; it can bend, it can align, it can gently guide a hand.  It’s a practice of attention that rejects the slow despair, the foundation of connection in a world too numb to care.  [Bridge] Step into another’s sky, not to fix, not to sway, just to widen your horizon in a humble human way.  Peace grows out of trust, and trust grows out of care; and the bravest kind of mercy is the mercy that stays there.  [Final Chorus] Real compassion isn’t soft, it’s an odyssey of heart. It’s the bravery to feel what could pull a world apart.  Call it foolish, call it foreign, still the strongest force we share; nothing’s more rebellious than the courage to care.  [Outro] Let them chant their tired slogans, we don’t borrow secondhand fear. Compassion isn’t weakness; it’s the brightest way to hear.  It’s the method, it’s the mirror, it’s the long, unbroken stare of a world that heals itself through the courage to care.  🕊️

_desc-yt: “Penguins in Shoes” is a SHOWsutra fusion swirl of conscious psychedelic gipsy trip-hop jazz lofi tracks with a dystopian wink. This song was inspired by Anatole France’s 1908 masterpiece “Penguin Island”, a satire so fresh so sharp it somehow still feels like it was written yesterdaze.   Anatole (i.e. Monsieur France:) took a flock of innocent penguins, accidentally baptized them into “humanity,” and used their bumbling new society to show how fear, vanity, power, myth-making, and herd logic à la ”Rhinoceros” all keep replaying in every era… including ours. It’s funny, it’s absurd, it’s painfully accurate, and delightfooly tender.  I love that tale, because it’s yet another “WTF is wrong with us?” novel, with a sweet absurdist stink of neo-realism in a world gone rotten bananas… It’s a quirky invitation to think, feel, and question authoritarianism, with cheeky, brave compassion—because critical clarity matters, and it’s true most cruelty is born from confusion, most dogma from fear, and most crowd madness from our longing to belong.  And my intention, with this song, is simply to bring a smile to my (and maybe your) day, and honor Anatole’s spirit—goofy, trippy, reflective—kinda like a cheeky little mirror held up to our collective wobble.  So, please do yourself a favor: read Penguin Island. It’s short, sharp, hilarious, unsettling, and kind. And a century later, it still explains more about the world than most wannabe pundits. And remember to enjoy the wobble along the way… may we all learn to slip with jester style 🙏  @bananasutra #originalsong #lyrics  [CHORUS] We’re penguins in shoes, Making up truths. Falling for news, Choosing our views. We slip, we refuse, We win, then we lose. But love cuts through, Penguins… in shoes. [Verse 1] Tu nous as dit regarde en face, Sans mensonge, sans carapace. Le monde n’explique pas ses lois, Mais il répond quand on est là.  Pas de sens tombé du ciel, Pas de rôle providentiel, Juste l’effort d’être vivant, Lucide, libre, maintenant.  [Refrain] La révolte, ça nourrit, Et l’absurde, ça sourit. Ça oui, c’est ça la vie, Vas-y, dis-lui oui.  [Verse 2] La beauté de l’absurde, C’est l’instant qui déborde. Un bonheur sans injoncture, Une joie sans mot d’ordre.  La vie, c’est des moments, Un éclat hors du temps. Peut-on être un saint sans dieu ? Oui, si l’on choisit d’être heureux.  [Verse 3] Quand l’injustice faisait loi, T’as choisi d’écrire, pas de te taire. Combat, l’encre contre l’effroi, Résister sans devenir sévère.  Ni bourreau, ni innocent pur, Juste humain, debout, responsable. Refuser la haine future Même quand le monde devient coupable.  [Bridge (KNOW + GROW + FLOW + GLOWsutra)] Entre nihilisme et illusion, J’choisis l’absurde en révolution. Le nihilisme abandonne, L’absurde, lui, me façonne.  [Refrain final] La révolte, ça nourrit, Et l’absurde, ça sourit. Ça oui, c’est ça la vie, Vas-y, dis-lui oui.  😘  Here's google translated this, if you're curious:  Rebellion nourishes the soul, And the absurd wears a smile. Yes, indeed, that is life; Go on, say "yes" to it!  Yes, I have a soft spot for Albert. Oh, but Albert, he is charming! Albert is far from being a stranger; Camus helps you truly live.  For if you really think about it, There is a great deal of common sense In the reality of nonsense, A true story of existence.  The beauty of the absurd, The joy of the moment, It changes everything; That is all.  Life is made of moments, A joy existing outside of time. But can one be a saint without a God? Why not simply choose to be happy?  Caligula is tragic, Yet he is also authentic. Men die; They are not happy.  Rebellion nourishes the soul, And the absurd wears a smile. Yes, indeed, that is life; Go on, say "yes" to it!

_desc-sc: Long story short: Seven sutras walked into a bar. The bartender said, "Why the long peel?" Ha…   Seven Sutras Gone Bananas is a SHOWsutra song, part of the “B.J. is for Banana Jokes songbook“, and an attempt at baking all seven sutras into one ripe song. Think of it as a gospel gone bananas, or the Ten Commandments revised into seven guiding beliefs, and compressed into one silly and radically sincere song... dripping truth, sipping groove, and nothing to prove. Obviously.  If you’re curious (like me), here's my bananasutra not-secret recipe for living a good life on Earth:  1. KNOWsutra (seek clarity): Ask all the questions. Learn that bananas come in many shapes. Agree on what's right and wrong, with radical honesty. First things first. 2. BLOWsutra (fight a-morality): Hey, you. Watch out for the banana peel. Fall on your ego. Then stand up, together, in unity. 3. SHOWsutra (rejoice in absurdity): Fool around like apes bone bananas, because love is light made of silly tender joy. We fool 'cause we feel. That's the medicine. 4. GROWsutra (blessed be curiosity): Dare to be brave. Breathe deeper. Open every door and window to evolve already, god damnit… because yes, that is the point of life, and so we must. 5. FLOWsutra (trust in serendipity): Tune in to the chaotic beat. Leap in space, across time, beyond fear, flying free… like a river caressing rocks, in lust for trust. 6. GLOWsutra (believe in felicity): Thank the rainbows in the clouds. Peel bananas like it's poetry. Because adopting the gratitude attitude is the key to happiness, and that shimmer? That's the glow. 7. BOWsutra (find spirituality in humility): Where grace meets gravity, in spirituality. Where we blush in wonder, and surrender to all we know we don't know. And then, it all starts again ∞  EPx13 flows like this: ▸ Avant-Garde Cello DUB (1)  ▸ Gipsy Fusion LOFI (2-6)  ▸ Post-Punk Cabaret BURLESQUE (7-11)  ▸ Banjo Bluegrass FOLK (12-13)  — @bananasutra #songlyrics   [Intro] Peel back the veil, babe, my fruit’s gone ripe, Seven slick secrets in a sutra rite, Drippin’ truth, sippin’ groove, Bananasutra got nothin’ to prove.  [Verse 1: KNOWsutra 1st Sutra = knowing through asking] One: KNOW, don’t show off, just grow wise, Ask, don’t mask, let the mind improvise, Bananas got forms that defy your plan, I’m peelin’ philosophy right in your hand.  [Verse 2: BLOWsutra speaks of absurd egos masquerades] Two: BLOW, beware of the slippery spin, Hey you! Watch out, peel on the floor again! Bananasutra booms with a rebel grin, Fall on your ego, that’s where we begin.  [Verse 3: SHOWsutra celebrates fool (not foul) play & self-expression] Three: SHOW, we shine like jesters divine, Ape gone wild on a burlesque line, Banana smile in a jelly-roll role, We fool ‘cause we feel, that’s the medicine for soul.  [Verse 4: GROWsutra is where we be brave, because yay, evolution] Four: GROW, breathe deep, baby, roots grow proud, Rise from the rind, sing brave and loud, Bananas be bold, fruit blessed on cue, I’m the priestess of peel. Hallelujah to you.  [Bridge: FLOWsutra oh la la, time for surrender & transcendence aka trust] Five: FLOW, time melts, the beat ticks slick, Heartbeat drips that cosmic click, Leap through space, no peel, no fear, Bananasutra floatin’ through atmosphere.  [Verse 5: GLOWsutra where gratitude means felicity] Six: GLOW, shimmer soft in the solar sigh, Velvet banana in a nebula sky, Gratitude glows under golden skin, Immunity born where the truth sinks in.  [Verse 6: BOWsutra humility & wonder or, the ultimate revelation] Seven: BOW, blush deep at the divine appeal, Magic banana, surreal, so real, Bend, not break, just kiss the light, Bananasutra bows to what shines bright.  [Outro gone banana] So peel me slow where the secrets hum, Each sutra sung, each layer undone, Bananasutra, the gospel’s clear, The joke, the joy, the love… all here.  — 🍌 Learn more on bananasutra.com

The Conquest of Happiness is a 2-songs EPx10 inspired by Bertrand Russell’s 1930 masterpiece—a philosophical field guide for ordinary people trying to build a life that feels real, meaningful, and free. This EP is an homage to Bertrand Russel, and a soundtrack for anyone who’s trying to stay awake, stay kind, stay curious, and stay human… Think of it as a humble and grateful love letter to curiosity, emotional honesty, and the kind of philosophy that makes you sit up straighter and breathe easier… with humor, compassion, and just enough sASS :)  WHAT IS THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS? Bertrand Russell wrote this book  because he saw ordinary people suffering unnecessarily—not from tragedy, but from habits of mind, toxic social pressures, and self-inflicted misery. He argued that happiness isn’t a mystery. It’s not a miracle. It’s a skill.
And he gave us a map. This EP is my humble attempt at translating that map into music.  SIDE A : “THE UNHAPPINESS DANCE” A song (x5) songs inspired by the forces that drain joy and distort the mind, i.e. the reasons why people tend to feel unhappy—namely, the emotional chaos, the self-sabotage, and the absurdity of modern misery. Russell’s #unhappiness list, simplified: 1. Competition: Always comparing yourself to others.
 2. Boredom / Excitement Extremism: Swinging between “numb” and “thrilled” without ever landing in contentment.
 3. Fatigue: Overwork, stress, and no margin for joy.
 4. Envy: Measuring your worth by what others have.
 5. Guilt & Moral Self-Torment:  Beating yourself up for being human.
 6. Fear of Public Opinion: Living your life under imagined surveillance.  SIDE B : “THE CONQUEST OF HAPPINESS” A song (x5) about what actually creates lasting well-being, what makes people truly happy. These songs waltz through the antidotes: curiosity, connection, creativity, pleasure, laughter, kindness, courage, and the everyday magic that makes life feel like life. Russell’s #happiness list, simplified: 1. Zest: Being genuinely interested in life.
 2. Affection: Love given and love received.
 3. Meaningful Work: Not necessarily glamorous, but engaging.
 4. Wide Interests: Multiple passions, not one obsession.
 5. Effort & Resilience: The willingness to grow, to try, to adapt.
 6. Impersonal Interests: Joy in things outside the self (nature, ideas, art).
 7. A Sense of Purpose: Living for something larger than ego.  WHY THIS MATTERS NOW? Because we’re living in a time of distraction, polarization, loneliness, and algorithmic noise that quietly eats away at our sense of self… Because people are anxious, burnt out, overstimulated, overwhelmed, and under-nourished in the soul. And because Russell’s wisdom—nearly 100 years old—feels like it was written yesterday, for the world we’re in right now.  ☰☰☰ NOTE: Lyrics matter, and I’d gladly share mine upon request, as always. But Soundcloud description length is limited, and for this EP, I wanted to tell you more about Bertrand instead of sharing lyrics, because he is a gift to humanity… and, in a world gone unhappy bananas, I hope he may help inspire you to find your path(s) to #happy, too. Look him up <3

"People seem good while they are oppressed, but they only wish to become oppressors in their turn: life is nothing but a competition to be the #criminal rather than the victim.”—Bertrand Russel  You may be tempted to argue this view of the world is too pessimistic, because many people choose empathy and justice over dominance. I don't completely disagree. That sure is a comforting worldview. And blessed be your voice... But(t) I’d argue that in hindsight, historically, Bertrand’s observation is in fact an accurate critique of how power does seem to corrupts human behavior. It’s depressing, yeah, because it’s true. And, if the current world order ain’t making you feel disillusioned with politics and mankind, well... perhaps you’re not thinking and feeling enough, heh?
  This is why so many of my songs keep circling back to ego—ego as THE root of all evils, i.e. all that BLOWs (and, in contrast, win-win kindness as the antidote). Because imho, as long as power and dominance are perceived as “winning strategies”, as long as the game of life is conceptualized as a series of finite transactional moves, the cycles of (criminal) cruelty simply will continue. Sigh.   I mean, for example, hello Murica. See what happens when pussy grabbing is normalized and excused, as an inconsequential puerile behavior? To say the least... #ahem   "Criminals (Bertrand Edition) " EPx15 flows JAZZ (1) ▸ BLUES (2) ▸ LOFI (3-9) ▸ Fado Techno Fusion WORLD (10-15)  — @bananasutra #songlyrics   [Intro] Bertrand Russel said life is nothing But an eternal criminal ring…  [verse] Criminals, Like life’s a game of bully king thrones, cold, cruel, People trapped by shady golden rules, Oh dear, let’s pray for ‘em criminals  (Criminals, criminals, criminals)  [verse] Yesterday, We hope the world would be a better way, But now we see it’s all a rigged display, Trumped by breaking news memes all day.  [chorus] Why we shrug, I don’t know, can’t we see? Hear me out, it’s not just me, We just can’t be trapped eternally, By criminals.  (Oh Criminals…)  [verse] Criminals, Setting traps, predators preaching dirty lies, Crimes of power acting in disguise, Worst… no one even dares to criticize!  [chorus] Why we shrug, I don’t know, can’t we see? Hear me out, it’s not just me, Games of lose-lose by denial… Damn, criminals!  (Criminals, criminals, criminals)  [outro] Criminals, Victims fates sealed by creepy villain’s claws, Felons only know to break ’n bend the laws Daddy dances with criminals, ooh  (Criminals, criminals, criminals)  — This is volume 4 of this song, rewritten to integrate Bertrand’s KNOWsutra wisdom. _desc-sc: Every breakup deserves a proper bow... Even the toxic ones. Especially the toxic ones.  This is a BOWsutra farewell letter to the worst lover I ever had: a skinny little liar in a paper dress who moved in when I was fifteen, never paid rent, and kept stealing my dopamine while swearing it was romance. We played libertine. She played me.  BOWsutra is the art of the bow: bowing out, bowing to the lesson, bowing gracefully toward the door. So here I bow, but(t) not to her. I bow to my lungs for forgiving me, to every craving for teaching me patience, and to that sad violin in the outro, whose bow does the weeping so I don't have to.  No sermon, no finger-wagging. Nobody ever quit because someone scolded them. You quit the day the romance finally smells like ashes in a tin.  Adieu, ma vieille reine toxique. The cage door was open all along.  18 takes, 8 moods, one goodbye: [01–03] Ethically Gipsy JAZZ [04] Weary Old School Banjo BLUES [05–06] Queen of Authentic Bluesy Dub FOLK [07–09] Poetry Bridges the DUB [10–12] Arabesk Hop Cabaret BURLESQUE [13–14] Oh Boy Accordion Circus BURLESQUE [15–16] Oh My Oh Why Accordion Cello INDIE [17–18] Cello Fiddle Piano Soul INDIE  ~  LYRICS  [Intro] Oh, goodbye, good old nicotine, Farewell, my bitter chemical dream…  [Verse 1] I met you when I was fifteen, You and I played libertine, I used to smoke like breathing in, Now I want you off my skin.  [Pre-Chorus] You stink like ashes in a tin, I won't let you back within.  [Chorus] Oh, nicotine, my old toxic queen, You filled the spaces in between, Always there when the world got mean, While stealing all my dopamine…  [Verse 2] My fingers itched to pull you in, Your yellow filter flickering, You haunt me like a deadly dream, The worst damn liar I've ever seen.  [Chorus] Oh, nicotine, my old toxic queen, You filled the spaces in between, Always there when the world got mean, While stealing all my dopamine…  [Bridge] You called it romance, I call it a scheme, A toxic ex in a nicotine dream, My lungs are healing, my head's more keen, I'm cutting you out like a bad movie scene.  [Outro] Farewell, oh, nicotine, A brand-new day can now begin, Can you hear that sad violin? I'm choosing life, and I'm gonna win.  Signed with love, Céline.  ~ bananasutra.com
